editorial:
Imagine traveling to the future only to find out your older self has completely panicked and run away from his own wedding! That is exactly the mess you get into here. You follow young Nobita and his robotic best friend Doraemon as they try to fix a huge disaster. The movie has a really warm, cozy vibe that reminds you of childhood, but it adds a lot of heart and some genuine tears. It is not just about gadgets and laughs; it is a story about family, growing up, and the promises we make to the people we love most.

What really works is how the movie balances the funny moments with the sad ones. The pacing is smooth, though some parts feel a bit slow until the big emotional payoff at the end. You will love the colorful animation and the way it handles the relationship between Nobita and his grandmother.
endingExplained: In the end, Nobita realizes that his future self ran away because he was too nervous and scared to face the happiness he deserved. After some heartfelt lessons and a bit of help from Doraemon, adult Nobita finds his courage. He returns to the wedding and finally marries Shizuka. The movie wraps up with a sweet moment showing that love and family are more important than fear, leaving you feeling happy and hopeful.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves touching stories about friendship and family.
